top_temples.name: Aranya Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Arrah; a Siddhapeetha and the temple after which the city (Ara) is named, includes a subsidiary shrine to Rama, Sita, Lakshman, and Hanuman.

top_temples.name: Mahamaya Temple, Arrah
top_temples.location_note: Arrah; draws visitors from across India.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Mandir, Arrah
top_temples.location_note: Arrah city; houses a black-stone Hanuman statue.

top_temples.name: Shiv Temple, Ramna Maidan
top_temples.location_note: Within Ramna Maidan (Babu Veer Kunwar Singh Ramna Maidan), one of Arrah's largest urban parks.

top_temples.name: Gayatri Mandir, Arrah
top_temples.location_note: On the main Ara-Bihiya road, near Ara collectorate.

top_temples.name: Ajgaivinath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sultanganj, Bhagalpur; a 2nd-century AD temple, the most famous and ancient temple in Bhagalpur.

top_temples.name: Champapur Digambar Jain Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Bhagalpur; one of five supreme Jain pilgrimage sites, dating back over 2,500 years.

top_temples.name: Budhanath Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Ganges in Bhagalpur; known for its large Shiva linga.

top_temples.name: Colganj Rock Cut Temple
top_temples.location_note: Colganj, Bhagalpur; ancient rock-cut carvings flourished under the Gupta Empire.

top_temples.name: Shiv Shakti Mandir, Bhagalpur
top_temples.location_note: Bhagalpur city.

top_temples.name: Shyama Kali Temple (Shyama Mai / Rameshwari Kali Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Built 1929 CE on the pyre of Maharaja Rameshwar Singh in Darbhanga; the city's most famous temple, lively during Navratri and the December Shyama Mai festival.

top_temples.name: Kankali Temple, Darbhanga
top_temples.location_note: Darbhanga; a centuries-old temple regarded as a major tantric site in North Bihar.

top_temples.name: Ahilya Asthan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Darbhanga; associated with the Ramayana legend of Ahilya's liberation by Rama.

top_temples.name: Manokamna Temple, Darbhanga
top_temples.location_note: Darbhanga city.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Darbhanga
top_temples.location_note: Darbhanga city.

top_temples.name: Deo Sun Temple (Deo Surya Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Deo, about 10 km southeast of Aurangabad; a 15th-century, 100-ft temple uniquely facing west toward the setting sun, major Chhath Puja site.

top_temples.name: Umga Sun Temple
top_temples.location_note: Umga village, near Deo; regarded as the second most important Chhath Puja temple in the region after Deo.

top_temples.name: Vishnupad Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gaya's central Hindu shrine; a 100-ft granite temple housing the footprint (Dharmasila) of Vishnu.

top_temples.name: Mahabodhi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bodh Gaya; UNESCO World Heritage Site marking where the Buddha attained enlightenment.

top_temples.name: Mangla Gauri Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Mangla Gauri Hill, Gaya; one of the 18 Shakti Peethas.

top_temples.name: Dungeshwari Cave Temples
top_temples.location_note: Near Bodh Gaya; cave shrines associated with the Buddha's pre-enlightenment austerities.

top_temples.name: Brahmayoni Hill Temple
top_temples.location_note: Brahmayoni Hill, Gaya; a hilltop pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Kapileshwar Temple (Kapileswarsthan)
top_temples.location_note: Madhubani district; the Shiva linga here is said to have been installed by sage Kapila.

top_temples.name: Somnath Mahadev Temple, Saurath
top_temples.location_note: Saurath village, Madhubani; local tradition holds this Shiva linga to be the same as the one from Gujarat's Somnath Temple, associated with Sita's legendary Swayamvar site.

top_temples.name: Sita Kund
top_temples.location_note: Vedivan/Madhuban Panchayat, outskirts of Motihari; a sacred pond where Rama's wedding procession is believed to have rested.

top_temples.name: Someshwar Nath Mahadev Temple, Areraj
top_temples.location_note: Areraj, about 30-40 km from Motihari; an ancient Shiva shrine known for its deep-set linga, major Shravani Mela pilgrimage.

top_temples.name: Modern Shiva Temple, Areraj
top_temples.location_note: Areraj, near Motihari; established 2002, local tradition holds the idols emerged naturally from the earth here.

top_temples.name: Kesaria Rama Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kesaria, about 50 km from Motihari; a large Ramayana-themed temple project begun in 2018.

top_temples.name: Motihari Station Mandir
top_temples.location_note: At the Motihari railway station in the city itself.

top_temples.name: Mundeshwari Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mundeshwari Hills, Kaimur district; ASI-dated to 108 AD, regarded as one of the oldest functioning Hindu temples in the world, Nagara-style architecture.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Shivalinga Shrine, Mundeshwari Complex
top_temples.location_note: A subsidiary shrine within the central part of the same Mundeshwari temple, alongside idols of Vishnu, Surya, and Ganesha; used here as the second entry since Mundeshwari's identity centers on this single temple.

top_temples.name: Garib Nath Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Muzaffarpur's oldest temple, called the 'Deoghar of Bihar'; especially busy during Shravan.

top_temples.name: Chhinmastika Mandir, Muzaffarpur
top_temples.location_note: Muzaffarpur city.

top_temples.name: Shri Rani Sati Mandir, Muzaffarpur
top_temples.location_note: A well-regarded temple within Muzaffarpur city.

top_temples.name: Maa Vaishno Devi Mandir, Muzaffarpur
top_temples.location_note: Muzaffarpur city.

top_temples.name: Devi Mandir, Muzaffarpur
top_temples.location_note: Muzaffarpur; regarded as one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.

top_temples.name: Surya Mandir, Surajpur Baragaon
top_temples.location_note: Surajpur Baragaon, about 1 km from the Nalanda University ruins; one of the 12 Suryadhams in India, alongside a notable 5-ft Parvati idol.

top_temples.name: Shiva Temple, Ramchandrapur
top_temples.location_note: Ramchandrapur, near the Nalanda ruins; legend associates the site with a visit by Krishna and Balarama.

top_temples.name: Mahavir Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Patna; the second-largest religious shrine in North India, one of Bihar's most visited temples.

top_temples.name: Patan Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Patna's oldest temple; one of the 51 Siddha Shakti Peethas.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Patna
top_temples.location_note: Patna; 84 pillars spread over 2 acres, one of the largest Radha-Krishna temples in Bihar and Jharkhand.

top_temples.name: Gayatri Mandir, Patna
top_temples.location_note: Patna city.

top_temples.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
top_temples.location_note: Patna; one of the holiest Sikh shrines, marking the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh.

top_temples.name: Puran Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: About 5 km from Purnia city; the district's oldest temple, major Navratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Kali Mandir, Purnia
top_temples.location_note: Purnia city; a significant local pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Kamakshi Sthan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Purnia city.

top_temples.name: Markandey Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: Purnia district.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Hanuman Mandir, Purnia
top_temples.location_note: Purnia city.

top_temples.name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple, Rajgir
top_temples.location_note: Rajgir, beside the seven hot springs of Saptadhara.

top_temples.name: Nandyavarta Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rajgir; marks the traditional birth location of Mahavira, houses a 4.5-ft idol in Padmasana posture.

top_temples.name: Mahendra Nath Temple, Mehdar
top_temples.location_note: Mehdar village, Siwan district; believed built by King Mahendra, major Mahashivratri pilgrimage.

top_temples.name: Panchmukhi Shivalinga Temple, Siwan
top_temples.location_note: Siwan; the linga displays faces of Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh, major Shivaratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Burhiya Mai Temple
top_temples.location_note: Gandhi Maidan, Siwan; especially busy on Saturdays.

top_temples.name: Anand Bagh Math and Sunder Bagh Math
top_temples.deity: Samadhi shrines of Swami Jaggannath Das ji and his guru
top_temples.location_note: Bakhri village, Siswan block, Siwan district.

top_temples.name: Baba Baijnath Dham, Siwan
top_temples.location_note: Siwan district; major Sawan month pilgrimage.

top_temples.name: Bawan Pokhar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the northern bank of the Bawan Pokhar tank in Vaishali; built during the Pala period, houses black basalt images including a four-headed Shivling.

top_temples.name: Shri Digambar Jain Mandir, Vaishali
top_temples.location_note: Behind the Bawan Pokhar Temple in Vaishali; an ancient Jain shrine distinct from the nearby Buddhist stupa.
